title: Personal Checking: ATM Fees, Foreign Transaction Fees and Operator Surcharge Rebates
content:
## Fees PCB charges on Personal Checking

- **Another bank's ATM in the United States.** Every withdrawal or balance inquiry draws the tier's domestic non-PCB ATM fee, booked as a fee entry naming that ATM debit as its source.
- **An ATM abroad.** Every withdrawal draws the tier's international ATM fee in place of the domestic non-PCB fee — one or the other, never both.
- **Foreign transactions.** Each debit card purchase made internationally, and each ATM withdrawal made abroad, also draws a foreign transaction fee: the item's amount multiplied by the tier's foreign transaction percentage, divided by one hundred, rounded half-up to the cent.
- **PCB's own ATMs** are free of any PCB charge.
- Where the tier's fee or percentage is 0.00, no entry is booked.

The tier applied to an ATM item is the tier on the account on the day that withdrawal posted.

## Rebates of operator surcharges

The surcharge that a non-PCB ATM operator adds to a withdrawal, whether domestic or international, is rebated within the statement cycle in the order the withdrawals posted. Each rebate equals that withdrawal's operator surcharge, subject to two per-cycle ceilings of the tier: a number of rebates and a running dollar total. The rebate that would carry the running total past the dollar ceiling is cut down to whatever room remains, and any later withdrawal in that cycle receives nothing. A rebate belongs to the cycle in which the rebated withdrawal posted. A withdrawal without an operator surcharge produces no rebate. Charges that PCB itself levies, whether for ATM use or for foreign transactions, are not surcharges and never qualify for this rebate.

## Calculation guide (hypothetical tier: three rebates, 9.00 USD ceiling, 2 percent foreign rate)

| Withdrawal (in posting order) | Operator surcharge | Running total before | Rebate |
|---|---|---|---|
| first | 3.50 | 0.00 | 3.50 |
| second | 0.00 | 3.50 | none (no surcharge) |
| third | 4.00 | 3.50 | 4.00 |
| fourth | 3.00 | 7.50 | 1.50 (cut to the remaining room) |
| fifth | 2.50 | 9.00 | none (ceiling reached) |

The fourth withdrawal uses the third and last rebate as well as the dollar ceiling.

Foreign fee on the same hypothetical tier: a purchase abroad of 47.35 USD yields 47.35 multiplied by 2 and divided by one hundred, which is 0.947, rounded half-up to 0.95 USD.
